reading.title: A different route home
reading.instructions: Read the story and choose the best answer.
reading.passage:
During my first summer working in Scotland, I stayed in a small village near the hills. One Saturday, I planned to take a bus to the coast. The driver told me that roadworks had stopped the service, but a local woman said there was another way. She pointed to a path behind the old church.

I followed it through a forest and past a stream. The walk was longer than I expected, so I began to worry that I had taken a wrong turn. Then I heard music. A family was having a picnic beside a small lake, and they showed me where the path joined the main road.

I reached the coast in time to watch the sun go down. I never did take that bus, but I discovered a beautiful place I would not have seen otherwise. When I visit again, I plan to walk the same route with a friend.

listening.title: An interview with a travel writer
listening.instructions: Listen to the interview and choose the correct answer.
listening.script:
Interviewer: Daniel, what made you start writing about travel?
Daniel: I kept a diary on a family trip when I was sixteen. My teacher read it and said I should write more. I didn’t take the idea seriously until a few years later.
Interviewer: Where did you go first for your work?
Daniel: To a town in the north of England. It wasn’t a famous place, but I wanted to show that interesting trips don’t have to be expensive or far away.
Interviewer: How do you choose where to visit?
Daniel: I ask readers to send ideas. They often know a small museum or walking path that isn’t in the guidebooks.
Interviewer: What do you find difficult?
Daniel: Travel delays can be frustrating, especially when I have a short deadline. I’ve learned to plan a second route, and I always carry a notebook in case my phone battery runs out.
Interviewer: What are you writing about now?
Daniel: A series about places you can visit by bus. It’s useful for people who don’t drive, and it helps me discover towns I might otherwise pass by.
